title: USMLE Step 2 Clinical Knowledge
description: Second of three USMLE licensing exams. Tests application of medical knowledge in patient care: internal medicine, surgery, pediatrics, OB-GYN, psychiatry. Reported as a three-digit score (mean ~245, passing standard ~214).

questions.promptMd: A 60-year-old man with diabetes presents with sub-sternal chest pressure for 1 hour. ECG shows ST elevation in II, III, aVF. Best next step?

options.label: A
options.text: Aspirin + heparin + door-to-balloon PCI within 90 min

questions.explanationMd: Inferior STEMI → emergent reperfusion. PCI within 90 min if available; else fibrinolysis. Always include ASA + anticoagulation.

questions.promptMd: A 45-year-old woman with fatigue and weight gain has TSH 18 mU/L (high), free T4 low. Most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanationMd: High TSH + low T4 = primary hypothyroidism. Hashimoto (anti-TPO antibodies) is the most common cause in iodine-replete countries. Treat with levothyroxine.

questions.promptMd: A patient on long-term PPIs is at increased risk of:

options.label: A
options.text: C. difficile infection, B12 deficiency, hypomagnesemia, hip fractures

questions.explanationMd: Chronic PPI use: ↑gastric pH → ↓absorption of B12, Ca, Mg + altered gut flora → C. diff risk + slight ↑ fracture risk.

questions.promptMd: A 28-year-old man with Crohn disease + iron-deficiency anemia + recent right-lower-quadrant pain has CT showing terminal ileitis. Initial pharmacologic therapy?
questions.explanationMd: Mild-moderate ileal Crohn: budesonide (low systemic activity) + 5-ASA. Step up to immunomodulators (azathioprine, biologics) for moderate-severe.

questions.promptMd: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) management priorities are:

options.label: A
options.text: IV fluids → potassium repletion → IV insulin → close monitoring

questions.explanationMd: Aggressive IV NS → check K+ (replete if low; hold insulin if K<3.3) → IV insulin gtt → q1h glucose. Bicarbonate only if pH < 6.9.

questions.promptMd: A 55-year-old man with chronic alcohol use develops sudden ascites + abdominal pain + bloody fluid on paracentesis. Most concerning diagnosis?
questions.explanationMd: In a cirrhotic, BLOODY ascites with sudden pain raises HCC with hemoperitoneum. SBP usually has neutrophil-rich (>250) but not bloody fluid.

questions.promptMd: First-line treatment for community-acquired pneumonia in an otherwise healthy outpatient (no comorbidities):
questions.explanationMd: IDSA: healthy outpatient CAP — amoxicillin 1g TID or doxycycline. Comorbidities → respiratory FQ or β-lactam + macrolide.

questions.promptMd: A patient on amiodarone develops dry cough + DOE + new pulmonary infiltrates. Most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanationMd: Amiodarone pulmonary toxicity (interstitial pneumonitis or fibrosis) is a feared side effect. Discontinue + steroids if severe.

questions.promptMd: A 72-year-old man with new heart failure + low-voltage ECG + 'speckled' myocardium on echo most likely has:
questions.explanationMd: Cardiac amyloidosis: thick walls but LOW voltage on ECG (a paradox), restrictive filling, sparkly speckled echo. AL or ATTR types.

questions.promptMd: Most common cause of new-onset atrial fibrillation in a 70-year-old?
questions.explanationMd: HTN is the most common AF risk factor in the elderly. Always screen TSH + look for structural heart disease.

questions.promptMd: A 65-year-old with COPD has chronic productive cough + new lethargy + ABG showing pH 7.30, PaCO₂ 65. Best initial step?
questions.explanationMd: Acute hypercapnic respiratory failure in COPD: BiPAP first-line if no contraindications. 100% O₂ can worsen hypercapnia.

questions.promptMd: Sudden onset RLQ pain + anorexia + low-grade fever + WBC 14,000 in a 22-year-old. Best initial imaging?

options.label: B
options.text: CT abdomen with contrast (or US in young/thin/pregnant)

questions.explanationMd: Suspected appendicitis: CT in adults; US first in children/pregnant for radiation avoidance. Treatment: appendectomy.

questions.promptMd: A trauma patient is hypotensive with positive FAST exam. Next step?
questions.explanationMd: Hemodynamically unstable + positive FAST → straight to OR for laparotomy. Stable + positive FAST → CT.

questions.promptMd: A 50-year-old man with painless jaundice + weight loss + palpable non-tender gallbladder (Courvoisier sign) most likely has:
questions.explanationMd: Courvoisier sign (palpable non-tender gallbladder + painless jaundice) classically suggests malignant biliary obstruction — pancreatic head most common.

questions.promptMd: Post-op day 5: a patient develops calf swelling + pain. Likely diagnosis + initial test?
questions.explanationMd: Post-op DVT presents with unilateral leg swelling/pain. Duplex US is the imaging of choice. Treat with anticoagulation if confirmed.

questions.promptMd: A patient 24h post-thyroidectomy has perioral tingling + Chvostek sign. Most likely cause?
questions.explanationMd: Post-thyroidectomy hypocalcemia from PTH disruption. Check serum Ca + albumin + PTH. Treat with IV/PO calcium ± vitamin D.

questions.promptMd: A 70-year-old with abdominal pain + a pulsatile mass + hypotension most likely has:
questions.explanationMd: Classic triad of ruptured AAA: pain + pulsatile mass + hypotension. Mortality is high; emergent operative repair.

questions.promptMd: A diabetic with a non-healing foot ulcer + probe-to-bone-positive likely has:
questions.explanationMd: Probe-to-bone in a diabetic ulcer has high specificity for osteomyelitis. MRI confirms; long-course antibiotics + debridement.

questions.promptMd: Post-op day 2: a patient has fever 38.4. Most likely cause?
questions.explanationMd: Five W's of post-op fever: Wind (atelectasis, day 1-2), Water (UTI, day 3-5), Wound (5-7), Walking (DVT/PE, 5+), Wonder drugs (anytime).

questions.promptMd: A 6-month-old infant has jaundice + acholic stools + dark urine + hepatomegaly. Most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanationMd: Persistent neonatal cholestasis + acholic stools + direct hyperbilirubinemia → biliary atresia. Urgent Kasai procedure within 60 days for best outcome.

questions.promptMd: A 4-year-old has a barking cough + inspiratory stridor + low-grade fever. CXR shows steeple sign. Best treatment?
questions.explanationMd: Croup (parainfluenza): barking cough + steeple sign. Dexamethasone for all; nebulized epi for moderate-severe. Most resolve without intubation.

questions.promptMd: A 2-week-old presents with projectile non-bilious vomiting + a palpable olive-shaped mass in the epigastrium. Most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanationMd: Pyloric stenosis: 3-6 weeks, projectile NON-bilious vomit, hypochloremic hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis. US confirms (thickened pylorus). Pyloromyotomy curative.

questions.promptMd: A 7-year-old has post-streptococcal hematuria + edema 2 weeks after a sore throat. Diagnosis?
questions.explanationMd: PSGN: hematuria + HTN + edema 1-3 weeks after pharyngitis or impetigo. Low complement (C3); ASO+. Self-limited; supportive care.

questions.promptMd: A 5-day-old infant has bilious vomiting. Initial study?
questions.explanationMd: Bilious vomiting in a neonate is malrotation with volvulus until proven otherwise. Upper-GI series is the gold standard ('corkscrew sign').

questions.promptMd: A 12-month-old with FTT has steatorrhea + recurrent pulmonary infections + sweat chloride 70 mEq/L. Diagnosis?
questions.explanationMd: CF: sweat chloride > 60 mEq/L is diagnostic. Pancreatic insufficiency + recurrent pulmonary infections + FTT in infants.

questions.promptMd: A 3-year-old presents with painless rectal bleeding. Most likely cause?
questions.explanationMd: Meckel: rule of 2s (2% population, 2 ft from ileocecal valve, 2 inches long, presents at age 2). Painless brisk bleeding from heterotopic gastric mucosa. Tc-99m pertechnetate scan.

questions.promptMd: A child with a 'slapped cheek' rash + low-grade fever has parvovirus B19. The most concerning complication is in:

options.label: B
options.text: Patients with hemolytic anemia (e.g., sickle cell) → aplastic crisis

questions.explanationMd: Parvovirus B19 infects RBC precursors (P antigen). Causes erythema infectiosum (Fifth disease) in children, aplastic crisis in chronic hemolytic anemia, hydrops fetalis in pregnancy.

questions.promptMd: Best initial test for evaluating a postmenopausal woman with new vaginal bleeding?
questions.explanationMd: TVUS first: endometrial thickness >4 mm or persistent bleeding → biopsy. <4 mm with single bleeding episode → reassuring.

questions.promptMd: Routine prenatal screen at 24-28 weeks includes:
questions.explanationMd: GTT for gestational diabetes screen at 24-28 wks. GBS swab is at 35-37 wks. Amnio + karyotype are diagnostic, not routine.

questions.promptMd: A 28-year-old with severe right-lower quadrant pain + amenorrhea x 7 weeks + β-hCG 1500 + empty uterus on US. Diagnosis?
questions.explanationMd: β-hCG > 1500-2000 ('discriminatory zone') without intrauterine pregnancy → ectopic until proven otherwise. Methotrexate vs. surgical management depending on stability + size.

questions.promptMd: Most appropriate management of severe preeclampsia at 36 weeks?
questions.explanationMd: Severe features at ≥34 weeks → delivery. MgSO4 for seizure prophylaxis. Steroids only if <34 weeks for fetal lung maturity.

questions.promptMd: A 30-year-old G2P1 has painless 3rd-trimester bleeding. US shows placenta covering the cervical os. Diagnosis?
questions.explanationMd: Placenta previa: PAINLESS bright-red 3rd-trimester bleeding. Diagnosed by US. Avoid digital exam. C-section at 36-37 weeks if persistent.

questions.promptMd: A 25-year-old woman has dysmenorrhea + dyspareunia + infertility. Laparoscopy reveals 'powder-burn' lesions on the peritoneum. Diagnosis?
questions.explanationMd: Endometriosis: ectopic endometrial tissue → cyclic pain + infertility. Powder-burn lesions + chocolate cysts are pathognomonic findings.

questions.promptMd: A 40-year-old G3P3 has heavy menstrual bleeding + uterine enlargement + 'Swiss cheese' appearance on US. Most likely?
questions.explanationMd: Leiomyomas are the most common benign uterine tumor. Heavy menses + bulk symptoms in reproductive-age women. Treatments range from medical (OCPs, GnRH agonists) to myomectomy/hysterectomy.

questions.promptMd: Postpartum hemorrhage most commonly results from:
questions.explanationMd: 4 T's of PPH: Tone (atony, ~80%), Trauma, Tissue, Thrombin. Initial: uterine massage + oxytocin + close monitoring.

questions.promptMd: First-line pharmacotherapy for major depressive disorder is:
questions.explanationMd: SSRIs (sertraline, escitalopram, fluoxetine) are first-line: efficacious + favorable side-effect + safety profile vs. older agents.

questions.promptMd: A patient on an SSRI develops fever + tremor + clonus + diaphoresis + agitation after adding a new medication. Most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanationMd: Serotonin syndrome: triad of mental status changes + autonomic instability + neuromuscular hyperactivity (clonus is hallmark). Stop serotonergic agents; consider cyproheptadine.

questions.promptMd: A patient with bipolar disorder is started on lithium. Required baseline labs include:

options.label: A
options.text: BUN/Cr, TSH, Ca, pregnancy test, ECG

questions.explanationMd: Lithium causes nephrogenic DI + hypothyroidism + hyperparathyroidism + Ebstein anomaly in fetus + ECG changes. Monitor levels + renal/thyroid function regularly.

questions.promptMd: A patient on haloperidol develops fever 39, rigidity, altered mental status, autonomic instability, CK 5000. Most likely diagnosis + treatment?

options.label: B
options.text: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome; stop neuroleptic + dantrolene/bromocriptine

questions.explanationMd: NMS: idiosyncratic reaction to dopamine antagonists. Triad: hyperthermia + rigidity ('lead-pipe') + autonomic instability + altered MS + elevated CK. Stop offending drug; supportive ICU care; dantrolene/bromocriptine.

questions.promptMd: A 70-year-old presents with fluctuating cognition + visual hallucinations + Parkinsonism. Most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanationMd: DLB: fluctuating cognition + visual hallucinations + Parkinsonism + REM sleep behavior. Antipsychotic SENSITIVITY (avoid haloperidol).

questions.promptMd: A 23-year-old with bulimia nervosa has hypokalemia + metabolic alkalosis. Mechanism?

options.label: B
options.text: Repeated vomiting → loss of HCl + volume contraction

questions.explanationMd: Vomiting loses HCl (alkalosis) + volume contraction → activated RAAS → ↑aldosterone → K+ wasting + further alkalosis.

questions.promptMd: ADHD first-line pharmacotherapy in a school-aged child is:
questions.explanationMd: Stimulants are most effective for ADHD core symptoms. Atomoxetine + α2-agonists (guanfacine, clonidine) are alternatives.
